problem: Documentation drift in a symbol this delta changed. The fix for r3-logic-w5-F-002 replaced the hand-off rule. A status row now anchors to its own parent: a Loading row anchors to `d:<parent>`, and a Show more row to the parent's last entry, and focus goes to the next row of that parent (handOff(), with the layout effect's `after.find(row => row.parent === lost.parent)`). Only an entry row still uses 'the row before it'. The component doc above `export function MetaprojectTree` still states only the old rule, 'the one after the row that preceded it'. That rule is the one the new test 'a focused Show more whose page lands with the children of the folder above it…' shows to be wrong: the row before Show more there is src's Loading row. The handOff doc and the layout-effect comment in the same file give the new rule, so one behaviour is now documented two ways.
impact: A reader of the component's public doc expects the pre-fix behaviour. A later change made to match that doc would bring back the r3-logic-w5-F-002 misfocus.
suggested_fix: Reword the last sentence of the doc so it defers to handOff, for example: '…when the focused row is replaced (its folder or next page loaded), focus goes to the row now at its place (`handOff`): a status row hands it to its own parent's next row, any other row to the row after the one that preceded it.'
evidence: MetaprojectTree.tsx:101-107 (component doc, unchanged by the delta) against handOff() at :958-965 of slice-02 (new) and the layout effect's target lookup (`lost.parent === undefined ? after[0] : after.find(row => row.parent === lost.parent)`), both changed in this delta. The new test in MetaprojectTree.dom.test.tsx expects focus on README.md, not on the row after the Loading row.

* when the focused row is replaced (its folder or next page loaded), focus goes to the row now at its
 * place: the one after the row that preceded it, when that row is still shown.

problem: A stale-snapshot read is parked as status 'stale' (or more: {status: 'stale'}) and only a change of `reload` re-reads it (the useEffect comparing loadedCatalog.current to reload is the sole caller of reread(scope, parent, 'stale')). `reload` is optional: a caller that omits it has no exit from a parked row, since ensure skips present folders, more refuses a set non-failed page, and retry acts only on 'failed'. The DOM-test Harness in MetaprojectTree.dom.test.tsx omits it; MetaprojectView passes reload: catalog.
impact: No user-visible defect at this head. The type does not encode the contract the round-3 major fix depends on, so a new caller or a refactor of the view's call can silently bring back the permanent Loading row.
suggested_fix: Make `reload` required and pass a value from the test Harness; or, when reload is undefined, treat 'stale' like 'failed' (offer Retry) so no state lacks an exit.
evidence: useMetaprojectTree.ts hook input type `reload?: unknown;`; effect `if (loadedCatalog.current === reload) return;` then reread(..., 'stale'). Callers: MetaprojectView.tsx (reload: catalog), MetaprojectTree.dom.test.tsx Harness (no reload).

problem: Ternary chain (a ternary inside a ternary) added by this delta. The layout effect that restores focus now picks the focus target with `const target = at < 0 ? undefined : (lost.parent === undefined ? after[0] : after.find(...)) ?? rows[at];`. The next line adds a third conditional (`target ? ... : elements[Math.min(...)]`). The three fallbacks are: no anchor, then the old index; an anchor without a parent, then the next row; an anchor with a parent, then the parent's next row, else the anchor itself. A reader has to unpack all three from one expression with a `??` between the branches.
impact: Readability. This is the code the round-3 focus finding (r3-logic-w5-F-002) was about, and the next reader checking a focus hand-off has to work through two nested conditionals and a nullish fallback in one statement.
suggested_fix: Move the target choice into a small named helper next to handOff, with early returns. For example: `function handOffTarget(rows: readonly Row[], anchor?: string, parent?: string): Row | undefined { const at = anchor === undefined ? -1 : rows.findIndex(row => row.id === anchor); if (at < 0) return undefined; const after = rows.slice(at + 1); const next = parent === undefined ? after[0] : after.find(row => row.parent === parent); return next ?? rows[at]; }`. The effect then reads `const target = handOffTarget(rows, lost.anchor, lost.parent);`.
evidence: slice-02 hunk @@ 104,217 of MetaprojectTree.tsx: the '+' lines `const at = ...`, `const after = rows.slice(at + 1);`, `const target = at < 0 ? undefined` / `: (lost.parent === undefined ? after[0] : after.find(...)) ?? rows[at];`, `const next = target ? elements.find(...) : elements[Math.min(lost.index, elements.length - 1)];`. The review-style checklist §3 rates a ternary chain as minor.
quote: (lost.parent === undefined ? after[0] : after.find(row => row.parent === lost.parent)) ?? rows[at];

problem: One concept has two names in the code this delta added. The hook's new input is called `reload` and typed `unknown`. Its doc says it 'Changes whenever the explorer loads its catalog'. The ref that remembers it in the same hook is `loadedCatalog`, and the effect compares `loadedCatalog.current === reload`. The caller passes `reload: catalog`. So the hook's public API names the value as an action, `reload`, while its body names it as a catalog. Neither name says what the value is: a token whose identity change triggers the re-read of parked stale reads. `reload` also reads like a callback here; Desktop's own `reload` in GitHubSettings.tsx:38 is a function.
impact: Readability. The input's purpose is only clear from its doc comment. A caller may expect to pass a function, and someone reading the effect has to match `loadedCatalog` to `reload` to see that they are the same value.
suggested_fix: Use one name that says it is a change token, both at the API and inside the hook. For example, `catalogLoad` (doc: 'a new value on every catalog load, same snapshot included') with ref `seenCatalogLoad`, or keep a generic `reloadToken` with ref `lastReloadToken`. Then the caller reads `catalogLoad: catalog`.
evidence: slice-02 hunk @@ 43,134 of useMetaprojectTree.ts: `reload?: unknown;` with doc 'Changes whenever the explorer loads its catalog (Refresh catalog included)'; hunk @@ 209,288: `const loadedCatalog = useRef(reload);` / `if (loadedCatalog.current === reload) return;` / `loadedCatalog.current = reload;`; MetaprojectView.tsx hunk @@ 738,782: `onStale: markStale, reload: catalog,`. keryx ctx rg -n '\breload\b' apps/desktop/src --all: 38 matches. Desktop uses `reload` both as a function (GitHubSettings.tsx:38 `const reload = () => {`) and as a counter dependency (RoutingDialog.tsx:38 `const [reload, setReload] = useState(0);`). The precedent is mixed, which is why this is minor and not higher.

problem: tdd-workflow.mdc Rule 3 (new branch with no test). This round adds the `stale` state and three branches that decide what a parked read looks like and whether it can be asked for again. (a) flatten renders a stale folder as a Loading row (`|| folder.status === "stale"`). (b) flatten renders a stale next page as loading (`loading: Boolean(folder.more)`, which replaces `folder.more?.status === "loading"`). (c) more() refuses a stale page (`(folder.more && folder.more.status !== "failed")`). None of the stale tests asserts the row while it is parked. 'a tree answer for another snapshot, or a stale-snapshot refusal, shows the stale banner and none of its rows' (MetaprojectView.dom.test.tsx:2139) and 'a next tree page answered for another snapshot is read again after Refresh catalog finds the same snapshot' (:2171) check, before Refresh catalog, only the banner, the absence of a 'Could not load.' row and the absence of Client/Late. Neither asserts a 'Loading…' row (or a busy Show more) under src or the root, and neither activates the parked Show more row. MetaprojectTree.dom.test.tsx:511 ('a next page refused as stale-snapshot…') also asserts only the onStale count, the absent Retry and README.
impact: Suppose (a) is dropped and the stale folder renders as an empty ready folder (no row at all). Or suppose (b) is reverted, so a parked page shows an actionable 'Show more' that more() then silently refuses. Or suppose (c) is reverted, so Enter on the parked row re-sends the cursor while the banner is up. In each case the listed tests stay green: each asserts only what is absent before the refresh and what is present after it. The operator's decision that a stale row 'shows as loading, banner only' has no test.
suggested_fix: In the MetaprojectView stale test, before clicking Refresh catalog, assert that the row under src is 'Loading…' (`treeRows().some(row => row.textContent === "Loading…")`). In the page twin, assert that the root's next-page row reads 'Loading…'. Then press Enter or click it, and assert that `explorer.treeCalls.filter(call => call.cursor === "page-2")` still has length 1 before Refresh catalog. That pins (a), (b) and (c) with the existing fixtures.
evidence: Test bodies in slice-02 (MetaprojectView.dom.test.tsx hunk @@ 2121,2207 @@; MetaprojectTree.dom.test.tsx :511 context). Test-title enumeration via `keryx ctx rg --all -n '^test\("[^"]*(stale|snapshot|reveal|elsewhere|Loading|wiki|Wiki)'` over both DOM suites: three stale-tree tests, none asserting a parked row. Mutants M4, M5, M6 would settle it; not run.

problem: tdd-workflow.mdc Rule 3 (new branch with no test). In the reveal effect, a step folder parked as `stale` makes the reveal wait instead of giving up. Without `|| folder.status === "stale"`, the stale folder has empty entries and no nextCursor, so the effect reaches `model.setHandled(scope, selection)`. That marks the selection handled, so after Refresh catalog re-reads the folder, the selection made elsewhere is never revealed. No test combines reveal with a stale answer. The three reveal tests (MetaprojectTree.dom.test.tsx:302, :327, :336; MetaprojectView.dom.test.tsx:2078) drive ready, paged and failed step folders only.
impact: The branch exists so that the reveal survives a stale step and Refresh catalog, and that is the case the round's major is about. If the branch is deleted, a graph-to-tree reveal that crosses a stale folder ends with the folder loaded and collapsed and the row not scrolled into view, and every test stays green.
suggested_fix: Add one MetaprojectView test. Make the first read of `src` answer for snapshot s2 (stale), as in the :2139 fixture. Select the src file from elsewhere (as at :2078). Then set the src answer to SRC_CHILDREN and click Refresh catalog. Assert that src is aria-expanded="true" and that the file's row is present (scrolled). Assert that a second elsewhere selection is not needed.
evidence: Test-title enumeration as in F1. The reveal tests' fixtures contain no stale-snapshot answer; the effect's handled path is visible in slice-02 MetaprojectTree.tsx hunk @@ 104,217 @@. Mutant M7 would settle it; not run.

problem: Mandatory under the lens's mutation rule: this gate was added in answer to the earlier round's major (r3-regression-w1-F-001). The reload effect re-reads parked reads in both scopes, but both recovery tests park a read in the graph scope only. The :2139 test does park a Wiki read: it expands 'Other' under a stale-snapshot refusal and asserts the banner. It then ends without Refresh catalog, so the Wiki half of the loop is never exercised. suggested_fix: Extend :2139 after its final assertions. Set `trees["s1|wiki|other|"]` to a ready answer with Guide, click Refresh catalog, flush, and assert that the banner is gone, Guide is present and no 'Loading…' row remains. Optionally park the Wiki read while Graph is on screen, to pin that the scope not shown is re-read too.
